summary: Verified the specific 'google api is already presented' LoadScript double-mount crash reported in iteration_104 does NOT reproduce anymore — code review confirms all 3 web map components (DestinationMapPicker.web.tsx, ActiveJourneyMap.web.tsx, AlertLocationMap.web.tsx) correctly use useJsApiLoader() with no `id` param, sharing the default loader singleton. Ran the full Head Out wizard flow (destination -> radius -> circle -> Start Journey) three times on web and never saw that crash or any 'google'/'presented' console/page error. HOWEVER, a different CRITICAL bug blocks the exact acceptance criterion requested: tapping 'Start Journey' does NOT land on the active /women/head-out session screen — it redirects back to Step 1 of the wizard. This is a stale-mount/stale-closure React state bug in head-out.tsx, unrelated to the LoadScript fix itself (confirmed by inspecting localStorage directly: the session IS persisted correctly, but head-out.tsx's session-read effect only runs once on first mount and never re-fires on router.replace back into an already-mounted screen instance). A manual hard-reload workaround at /women/head-out does show the active session screen rendering cleanly with no crash, confirming the LoadScript fix is sound in isolation — but normal in-app navigation never reaches it. Also found ActiveJourneyMap never mounts in this environment regardless, because EXPO_PUBLIC_GO1C_LIVE_ROUTE is unset/false in frontend/.env, gating the component off entirely — so the 'map actually renders a real map' criterion could not be visually confirmed either way. Backend health and login both verified 200.

integration_issues.flow: Head Out wizard Step 3 (circle.tsx) -> tap 'Start Journey' (headout-start-journey) -> active /women/head-out session screen
integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL — reproduced on 3 separate full end-to-end attempts: tapping 'Start Journey' does NOT navigate to the active session screen. It lands back on /women/head-out/destination (Step 1 of 3) instead. Confirmed via localStorage inspection that circle.tsx DOES correctly write the session to AsyncStorage/localStorage ('ws_head_out_session' key present and valid both immediately and 2.5s after the tap, with destination/radius/lat/lng all correct) — so this is NOT a data-loss bug. Root cause: head-out.tsx's session-loading `useEffect(() => {...}, [])` (empty deps, mount-only) already ran once earlier when the user first visited /women/head-out (before any session existed, redirecting them into the wizard) and set session=null. When circle.tsx later calls `router.replace('/women/head-out')`, Expo Router reuses the already-mounted head-out.tsx screen instance rather than remounting it, so the mount-only effect never re-fires to pick up the now-written session from storage — the stale `session=null` state immediately triggers the OTHER effect at line 273 (`if (!loading && !session) router.replace('/women/head-out/destination')`), bouncing the user straight back to Step 1. WORKAROUND CONFIRMED: manually hard-reloading the page at /women/head-out (bypassing the stale component instance) DOES show the active session screen correctly ('Session active', destination, countdown timer, no crash, no Google Maps error) — proving the underlying LoadScript fix is correct, but this stale-session-effect bug fully blocks the normal in-app flow from ever reaching that screen.

Could not visually confirm 'ActiveJourneyMap renders a real map with destination marker + arrival radius circle' as requested, because the component is gated by `{GO1C_LIVE_ROUTE_ENABLED && hasDestCoord && <ActiveJourneyMap/>}` in head-out.tsx, and EXPO_PUBLIC_GO1C_LIVE_ROUTE is not set in frontend/.env (so the flag evaluates false). Even with a valid destination pin (confirmed lat/lng 28.6139/77.2098 in the persisted session) and reaching the active screen via the hard-reload workaround, no map testID (headout-active-map) ever appeared in the DOM — purely because of this feature flag being off, unrelated to the LoadScript fix. The map DOES render correctly and without the double-LoadScript crash on the destination.tsx wizard step (DestinationMapPicker, real Google tiles around Central Secretariat/Connaught Place, Delhi, confirmed visually).

action_items: CRITICAL — fix head-out.tsx's stale session-read effect: the `useEffect(() => {...}, [])` that loads the session from AsyncStorage on mount needs to also re-run when navigation returns to this screen after circle.tsx writes a new session (e.g. add a route param/key change to force remount, use useFocusEffect from expo-router/react-navigation instead of a mount-only effect, or have circle.tsx pass the session via navigation params so head-out.tsx doesn't rely purely on a stale mount-time AsyncStorage read). This is what's currently preventing 'Start Journey' from ever visibly landing on the active countdown screen — the exact scenario this whole review round was meant to verify end-to-end.

Once the above navigation bug is fixed, re-verify the full Start Journey -> active screen transition via normal taps (not the hard-reload workaround used here) to get a clean pass/fail on the originally-reported LoadScript crash in the real user flow.

Decide whether EXPO_PUBLIC_GO1C_LIVE_ROUTE should be enabled in this preview's .env so ActiveJourneyMap can actually be exercised/visually verified going forward — right now it's impossible to confirm the active-journey map renders correctly (with or without the LoadScript fix) because the feature flag keeps the component from ever mounting.

Clean up the hundreds of duplicate 'QA Recipient Scoped' trusted-circle test entries polluting circle.tsx's Step 3 list (data hygiene issue from prior test sessions, not part of this fix, but makes manual QA of that screen impractical).

AlertLocationMap.web.tsx (guardian/alert flow) was not reached in this round per the request's stated lower priority — code review shows it correctly uses the same shared useJsApiLoader pattern as the other two, so it should be safe, but wasn't runtime-verified.

Could not re-confirm the rest of the requested regression sweep (admin-issues status dropdown, Evidence Vault, Guardian Journey public status page) due to time spent isolating the critical navigation bug above — Issue Reporter FAB presence was spot-checked and is still present on /women pages.
critical_code_review_comments: The useJsApiLoader refactor across all 3 web map components (DestinationMapPicker.web.tsx, ActiveJourneyMap.web.tsx, AlertLocationMap.web.tsx) is implemented correctly and consistently — no `id` param passed anywhere, so all 3 share the default '__googleMapsScriptId' loader singleton as intended. This part of the fix is sound.

head-out.tsx (1316 lines, already flagged oversized in iteration_104) has a real architectural issue independent of file size: its session-loading effect assumes the screen will always be freshly mounted when a session exists, which is false under Expo Router's screen-reuse behavior for router.replace within the same route group. Any future session-mutation flow that writes AsyncStorage then navigates back to this screen (not just circle.tsx's Start Journey) is at risk of hitting the same stale-state bug.

circle.tsx's Trusted Circle recipient list has no dedupe/pagination and is clearly rendering unbounded, unfiltered test data (hundreds of 'QA Recipient Scoped' rows) — worth adding at minimum a reasonable limit or empty-state styling guard so a polluted dataset doesn't make the screen unusable.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The LoadScript->useJsApiLoader fix itself is correct and the exact crash symptom from iteration_104 ('google api is already presented') no longer reproduces anywhere I tested, including a workaround that force-reaches the active session screen. Do NOT re-litigate that part. The NEW blocker is purely a React/Expo-Router state bug in head-out.tsx's session-loading useEffect (empty deps, never re-runs on route reuse) — fix that first, then redo the full normal-tap Start-Journey flow to get a true end-to-end pass/fail. Also remember EXPO_PUBLIC_GO1C_LIVE_ROUTE is off in this env's .env, so ActiveJourneyMap literally cannot be seen rendering until/unless that flag is turned on — don't mistake that for a LoadScript regression if you see no map on the active screen.
rca_of_issue: Session persistence works correctly (verified via localStorage.getItem('ws_head_out_session') immediately and 2.5s after the Start Journey tap — valid JSON with destination/radius/startTime/lat/lng all present). The bug is a stale React closure: head-out.tsx's `useEffect(() => { ...AsyncStorage.getItem(SESSION_KEY)...; setSession(...) }, [])` runs ONLY on first mount of that screen component. The user's very first visit to /women/head-out (before starting any journey) triggers this effect, finds no session, sets session=null, and a second effect (`if (!loading && !session) router.replace('/women/head-out/destination')`) immediately redirects them into the wizard. Later, after completing the wizard, circle.tsx calls `router.replace('/women/head-out')` — Expo Router's native-stack-style navigation reuses the already-mounted head-out.tsx instance instead of unmounting/remounting it, so the mount-only effect never re-fires, leaving the component's `session` state stuck at its original null value. That stale null immediately re-triggers the redirect-to-destination effect, bouncing the user back to Step 1 even though the newly-written session is sitting correctly in storage the whole time. Reproduced 3/3 attempts. Mitigation: replace the mount-only load effect with a focus-based reload (e.g. expo-router's useFocusEffect, or re-run on a route param change) so the screen re-reads AsyncStorage every time it's navigated to, not just on first mount.
